seed_ledger.name: Mustang Draw I and Mustang Draw II
seed_ledger.reason: Two gas processing plants in Stanton, Texas, with no pipe and no data center tie. Energy Transfer's fourth quarter 2025 and second quarter 2026 results describe them as fully contracted processing plants, phase one in service June 2026 and phase two due fourth quarter 2026. Oracle Abilene and CloudBurst gas deals are separate supply contracts. A TCEQ search found only a federal operating permit form for a Mustang Cryo Plant with no data center customer. Searches run: 6. Sources checked: EIA row (power demand only), Energy Transfer 8-Ks and earnings releases (plant capacity and timing only), TCEQ air permit search (no data center), trade press and Energy Transfer data center deal coverage (separate projects), Texas Railroad Commission not reachable by search (not confirmed).

evidence.note: not verified by fetch; Energy Transfer first quarter 2025 release naming the Midland Basin plant

seed_ledger.name: WT-0 Compressor Station Project
seed_ledger.reason: Length 0 compression-only. FERC docket CP25-37-000: one 13,220 hp compressor in Chaves County, New Mexico, 80,000 Dth/d firm service from the West Texas Lateral Central Zone to the Panhandle Lateral, cost about $52 million, shipper named as ETC Marketing, Ltd. Environmental assessment noticed August 2025. Open season 2024 lists no end user. The only nearby data center found is Zenith Volts, 20 miles south of Roswell, which plans on-site solar with gas generators for backup, but no source links the compressor to it. Searches run: 8. Sources checked: Federal Register notices (shipper ETC Marketing, no data center), Transwestern open season PDF (15 year term, no end user), FERC environmental assessment notice (no data center), Zenith Volts coverage (gas backup only, no pipeline named), NMED public notices (existing Roswell Station 9 permit only), Energy Transfer notices (maintenance only).

seed_ledger.name: Burr Computer Environments Energy Center (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND. No source names a gas supplier or pipeline for the Cedar Creek, Bastrop County site. Burr Computer Environments is a Houston-area data center design-build firm; searches found no Texas project under its name. The Cedar Creek campus reported in news is Project Longhorn (Pacifico Energy, 710 MW on-site turbines for 490 MW IT load, tenant reported as Anthropic, state permit pause in September 2026), and it may or may not be the same site. A separate MPH Bastrop Peakers permit (178585) is an existing power plant, not this one. Nearest GGIT lines are the Texas Intrastate System (4.4 km) and Atmos Pipeline Texas. Searches run: 9. Sources checked: DCD and CBS Austin coverage (turbines and permit pause, no gas supplier), TCEQ pending notices (MPH Bastrop only), Burr company listings (no Texas project), Texas Comptroller data center list (no Burr), county and tax-abatement news (withdrawn, no gas detail), Railroad Commission and FERC (nothing found).

evidence.note: Cedar Creek campus and on-site gas turbines, no supplier named
